name: The Rt Hon Lord Hague of Richmond
bio: Lord William Hague of Richmond is Chancellor of the University of Oxford and one of the United Kingdom's most distinguished statesmen. A graduate of Magdalen College, Oxford, and former President of the Oxford Union, he served for 26 years in the House of Commons, including as Secretary of State for Wales, Leader of the Conservative Party, First Secretary of State, and Foreign Secretary. Throughout his career, he has been closely engaged with issues of international trade, economic competitiveness, energy security, geopolitics, and Britain's role in the global economy. Since leaving frontline politics, he has remained active in business and public policy and has co-authored reports with Sir Tony Blair advocating for a stronger national focus on science, technology, and innovation. An award-winning historian, author, and Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature, Lord Hague brings a unique perspective on the intersection of geopolitics, industrial policy, and national prosperity. He was elected Chancellor of the University of Oxford in 2024 and assumed office in February 2025.

name: Dr Monica Gorman
bio: Dr Monica Gorman is Co-President (acting) of Crowell Global Advisors, and a former senior White House official whose work sits at the intersection of industrial policy, global trade, supply chain resilience, and corporate strategy. She served as Special Assistant to the President for Manufacturing and Industrial Policy from 2022 to 2025, where she helped establish the White House Council on Supply Chain Resilience and led the U.S. Supply Chain Disruptions Task Force. She previously served as Deputy Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Manufacturing, working on the competitiveness of strategically important sectors including semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, aerospace, automotive, nuclear, and solar energy. Before entering government, she held senior leadership roles at New Balance, American Eagle Outfitters, and Gap Inc., with responsibility for trade, compliance, sustainability, and global supply chains. Dr Gorman earned her M.Phil. and D.Phil. in Politics from the University of Oxford, where she was affiliated with St Edmund Hall and Nuffield College.

name: Angela Garcia Calvo
bio: Angela Garcia Calvo is Assistant Professor at the University of Reading. Her research studies how governments and firms work together to transform capitalisms and shape the direction of technological change. Specific topics include industrial-innovation policy, the platform economy and state-firm relations. Garcia Calvo's ongoing project Empowering Europe asks how Europe can generate new technological capabilities to generate prosperity, guarantee security and maintain a meaningful position in the global sphere.

name: Diane Coyle
bio: Diane Coyle is the Bennett Professor of Public Policy at the University of Cambridge and a member of the UK Government's Industrial Strategy Council. Her research focuses on productivity, the digital economy and AI policy, and economic measurement. She has been writing about the effects of digital technologies since her first book, The Weightless World, in 1997. The underlying motivation for all her work is the question: what does it mean for the economy to improve, and who benefits?

name: Annabelle Gawer
bio: Annabelle Gawer is a Chaired Professor in Digital Economy and Director, Centre of Digital Economy (CoDE) at the University of Surrey. A world-class academic pioneer in platform strategy, Professor Gawer's seminal research offers insights into the strategic management of platforms and the governance of their innovation ecosystems by exploring systematically the interaction between economic forces, organizational dynamics, and technological design.

name: Helena Malikova
bio: Helena Malikova is a European Union civil servant with the Directorate General for Competition (DG COMP) at the European Commission. She is currently leading the directorate's work on intelligence gathering and investigations and is researching the valuation of strategic M&A facilitated by foreign governments. She has published on the geopolitics of artificial intelligence and conflicts of interest among antitrust economists, academics and economic consultancies advising on regulation.

name: Mehdi Montakhabi
bio: Mehdi Montakhabi is Associate Scholar at Saïd Business School, University of Oxford. His research examines how nascent ecosystems emerge and scale in uncertain, highly regulated, and state-shaped markets, with a particular focus on commercialization in the space economy. He is also the founding organiser of the Academy of Management PDW on the space economy.

name: Dr Paul Bate
bio: Dr Paul Bate is the former Chief Executive Officer of the UK Space Agency, where he led the UK's civil space agency in advancing space science, commercial growth, and the use of space for economic, environmental, and societal benefit. In his role he oversaw national efforts to support R&D, space infrastructure, and the UK's role in international space activity.

name: Rob Desborough
bio: Rob Desborough is General Partner at Seraphim Space and Chair and co-founder of the Seraphim Space Accelerator. He has played a central role in building Seraphim's early-stage Space-Tech investment platform and supporting high-growth ventures across the space sector. His work focuses on identifying, backing, and scaling companies developing technologies and applications in areas such as communications, Earth observation, climate, defence, infrastructure, and space-enabled data.

name: Nigel Chandler
bio: Nigel Chandler is Head of Sales / Global Business UK at Airbus Defence and Space, where he leads customer engagement across UK defence and space markets. He works to connect advanced space capabilities with government, institutional, and commercial customers. His background spans customer strategy, large-scale programme development, and the translation of complex technological systems into market and mission needs.

name: Raja Roy
bio: Raja Roy is an Associate Professor of Innovation and Entrepreneurship at the Martin Tuchman School of Management, New Jersey Institute of Technology. His research focuses on technological innovation, breakthrough invention, and disruptive change in high-technology industries, including spacecraft and space-related systems.

name: John Gray
bio: John Gray is a Dean's Distinguished Professor, and the Chair of Operations and Business Analytics Department at Fisher College of Business, The Ohio State University. He is currently the PI on a subaward grant from the U.S. Department of Defense, charged with examining global pharmaceutical supply chains. Prior to pursuing his PhD, John worked for eight years in operations management at Procter & Gamble. He was co-PI of a contract with the FDA, part of a major FDA subaward, and co-PI on an NSF grant. John is also the past president of the Industry Studies Association.

name: Dr. Markus Felgenhauer
bio: Dr Markus Felgenhauer is Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer of QYOBO, a live intelligence platform providing data-driven insights into global pharmaceutical supply chains. QYOBO integrates hundreds of data sources to deliver transparency and live intelligence on manufacturing networks, compliance risks, pricing dynamics, and supply chain vulnerabilities across the pharmaceutical industry. Before founding QYOBO in 2019, Markus worked at McKinsey & Company, where he focused on the pharmaceutical sector. At QYOBO, Markus leads strategy, product innovation, and commercial development. His work focuses on bringing greater transparency and intelligence to pharmaceutical supply chains.

name: Damien Holly
bio: Damien Holly is VP, Head of Global Supply Chain at SERB Pharmaceuticals. Damien has extensive experience in supply chain and operations management, having served as the Chief Operations & Quality Officer at Provepharm Life Solutions and worked at Novartis as the Head of Supply Chain for the Sandoz Division. He also held the position of Director of Global Supply Chain at Hexcel Corporation, Director of European Supply Chain and Technical Services at Mundipharma International, and had various roles at Pfizer, including Director of Global Supply Chain Processes and Director of EMEA Supply Chain.

name: Mujaheed Shaikh
bio: Mujaheed Shaikh is Professor of Health Governance at the Hertie School, Berlin. His research concentrates on the field of health economics and management with a focus on health expenditures, hospital efficiency and competition, and health insurance. Mujaheed also has a keen interest in policy issues related to international donor funding for diseases and health in developing countries. Prior to joining the Hertie School, Mujaheed was employed at the Health Economics and Policy Division of Vienna University of Economics and Business. He has published in top field journals and has won several international awards.

name: Daniel Erian Armanios
bio: Daniel Erian Armanios is the BT Professor and Chair of Major Programme Management at Saïd Business School and a Professorial Fellow of St Anne's College. He also holds a Courtesy Appointment with the Department of Engineering Science. Daniel's research integrates civil engineering and organisational theory to better understand how organisations coordinate to build, manage, and maintain infrastructure amidst complexity. His work is published in leading outlets across the engineering and social sciences, and he has consulted and served on various panels and advisory boards for organizations such as the US National Academy of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, UNDP, and the US Department of Transportation.

name: Alison Baptiste CBE CEng FICE
bio: Alison Baptiste CBE CEng FICE is a Director in the National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority in the Treasury, the government centre of expertise for project delivery. She drives standards, improvements and pace in government's biggest and riskiest projects. Her portfolio covers infrastructure and service delivery in Defence, Digital, Health, Education, Welfare, Home Office, Justice and Tax. She also leads the cross-government forum on Transformation programmes. Prior to this Alison led operational delivery in the Environment Agency and received a CBE for her leadership responding to nationwide flooding. Alison also holds non-executive roles in the engineering profession and leisure industry.

name: Jim Hall FREng FRS
bio: Jim Hall FREng FRS is Professor of Climate and Environmental Risks in the University of Oxford. Prof Hall is internationally recognised for his research on risk analysis and decision making under uncertainty for infrastructure systems, water resource systems, flood and coastal risk management and adaptation to climate change. Professor Hall is a member of the Prime Minister's Council for Science and Technology. He was a Commissioner of the National Infrastructure Commission until 2025 and was President of the Institution of Civil Engineers for the year 2024-25. He was a member of the UK independent Committee on Climate Change Adaptation from 2009-2019, and was Chair of the Science Advisory Committee of the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis from 2020-22.

name: Julia Pyke CBE
bio: Julia Pyke CBE is a senior infrastructure leader with extensive experience in the development, financing and delivery of nationally significant infrastructure projects. She joined Agilia Infrastructure Partners as Executive Chair in April 2026. She served as Joint Managing Director of Sizewell C, the new nuclear power station under construction in Suffolk. Julia joined the project in 2017 as Development Director and later became Joint Managing Director, stepping down in December 2025. Prior to that, she spent over two decades at Herbert Smith Freehills, where she became a senior partner and Head of Power and Renewables for Europe. She currently serves as a Clean Power Commissioner for the UK Government and a non-executive director of Studsvik. Julia is a Fellow of the Energy Institute and the Nuclear Institute. She was awarded a CBE in the 2026 King's Birthday Honours for her services to the energy industry.

name: Chetan Kotur FREng
bio: Chetan Kotur FREng, an Automotive Engineer by background, is Head of Technology and Innovation at Laing O'Rourke. His career started with designing cars at Volvo Cars in Gothenburg, Sweden, before accelerating the global shift to sustainable electric mobility by starting up and launching the electric car brand Polestar. At Laing O'Rourke, he leads the team researching and developing transformative innovations in modern methods of construction focused on improving productivity, safety and sustainability on the complex buildings and infrastructure projects Laing O'Rourke delivers for its clients. In 2025, Chetan was elected as one of the youngest ever Fellows of the Royal Academy of Engineering.

name: Travis Mosier
bio: J. Travis Mosier is a technology, semiconductor, and global policy expert with a distinguished track record in spearheading federal initiatives that have improved market access, increased exports, enhanced the domestic investment climate, and strengthened supply chain resiliency. Mr Mosier serves as an Executive Advisor for Technology Partnerships, Public Policy & Strategy at mySilicon Compass, LLC, a strategic consulting practice that engages clients seeking to advance technological competitiveness, grow international sales and market share, create and foster public-private partnerships, and expand jobs, advanced manufacturing, and research and development investments in emerging growth sectors in the United States.

name: Sebastian Weiske
bio: Sebastian Weiske is Senior Manager Strategy Development at Infineon Technologies, a global semiconductor company serving automotive, power-management and Internet of Things markets. He leads macroeconomic and market-intelligence activities within Corporate Strategy, advising senior management on global economic trends, geopolitical developments and market shifts affecting the semiconductor industry. Before joining Infineon, he worked as a macroeconomist and policy adviser at the German Council of Economic Experts. He holds a PhD in Economics from Goethe University Frankfurt.

name: Jagjit Singh Srai
bio: Jagjit Singh Srai is Professor of Manufacturing and Head of the Centre for International Manufacturing at the University of Cambridge's Institute for Manufacturing. His research focuses on the design and operation of global supply chains, particularly the impact of new production and digital technologies on supply chain configuration and resilience. He has published over 100 journal articles, secured major research funding from UKRI, Europe, and industry, and serves on international initiatives including the World Economic Forum's Advanced Manufacturing Council, where he was Co-Chair from 2019-2025. Prior to academia, he held senior supply chain and technical leadership roles at Unilever. He holds degrees from Aston University and the University of Cambridge and is a Chartered Engineer and Fellow of the Institution of Chemical Engineers.

name: Edward Anderson
bio: Edward Anderson is the Betty and Glenn Mortimer Centennial Professor of Business at the University of Texas at Austin's McCombs School of Business. His research focuses on supply chain innovation, information systems, industrial policy, AI adoption, B2B platforms, and critical minerals. He has studied industries including automotive, electronics, software, and healthcare. Anderson has appeared in major media outlets including the BBC, Associated Press, Yahoo, Fortune, and Fox News, and has testified before the Texas Senate on supply chain disruption. A Fellow of the Production and Operations Management Society, he is also a research affiliate at MIT Sloan. He has authored more than 40 research articles and co-written The Innovation Butterfly and Operations Management for Dummies. Before academia, he worked as a product development engineer at Ford Motor Company and holds degrees from Stanford University and MIT.

name: Nitin Joglekar
bio: Nitin Joglekar is the John F. Connelly Endowed Chair in Management at the Villanova School of Business and convener of its Human-Centric and Agentic AI Lab. His research examines AI context estimation, agentic data platforms, AI guardrails, workflow reconfiguration, and industrial policy, with applications in critical minerals, financial services, and retail supply chains. He has more than 20 years of experience in the energy and IT sectors and has founded, advised, and consulted with venture-backed startups and established firms on AI, business strategy, and data platforms. Professor Joglekar serves as Department Editor for Digital Platforms, Innovation and Transformation at Production and Operations Management. He holds a BTech (Hons) from IIT and master's and doctoral degrees from MIT.

name: Professor Emeritus Sir Mike Gregory CBE, FREng
bio: Following an early career in industry, Professor Emeritus Sir Mike Gregory CBE, FREng was a founder member of the team that established the University of Cambridge's Institute for Manufacturing, linking science, engineering, management and policy while integrating education, research and practice. He retired as Head of the Manufacturing and Management Division in the University of Cambridge's Department of Engineering and as Head of the Institute for Manufacturing. He now chairs the Babbage Policy International Forum.

name: Professor Julia Sutcliffe
bio: Professor Julia Sutcliffe was appointed Chief Scientific Adviser at the Department for Business and Trade in February 2023. She provides science and engineering advice and independent challenge to ministers and senior officials, champions evidence-based decision-making, and builds internal scientific capability. She works with the network of departmental Chief Scientific Advisers and the Government Office for Science on cross-government issues. Previously, she was Chief Technologist at BAE Systems. She is an Honorary Professor in Computer Science at the University of Manchester, a Chartered Engineer, and a Fellow of the Royal Academy of Engineering and the Royal Aeronautical Society.

name: Eoin O’Sullivan
bio: Eoin O'Sullivan is the Babbage Fellow of Technology and Innovation Policy and Director of the Centre for Science, Technology and Innovation Policy at the University of Cambridge's Institute for Manufacturing. Since joining the Institute in 2007, he has researched how science and engineering R&D is translated into new technologies, industries and economic wealth. His policy work has included studies for UK government departments and research agencies, as well as work with the OECD, European Commission, United Nations Industrial Development Organization and US National Academies.

name: Michael A. Lewis
bio: Michael A. Lewis is Professor of Operations Management at the University of Bristol. His research examines how firms and industries build capabilities, manage innovation, and respond to technological and geopolitical change. He is co-author of the textbook Operations Strategy and has worked with industry and policymakers on manufacturing competitiveness, supply-chain resilience, and emerging technologies. His current work focuses on the evolution of critical industrial capabilities and the resilience and security of complex supply networks.

name: Saurabh Bansal
bio: Saurabh Bansal is Professor of Supply Chain Management at the Smeal College of Business, Pennsylvania State University, and Director of Research at Penn State’s Center for Supply Chain Research. His research examines supply chain and operations management, with a focus on decision-making under risk and uncertainty, forecasting, analytics, and how managers perceive and respond to operational uncertainty. He works with firms to develop data-driven forecasting and optimisation models, and his research spans agribusiness, remanufacturing, circular economy systems, retail operations, and supply chain risk.

name: Laura Dupin
bio: Laura Dupin is Assistant Professor of Entrepreneurship and Innovation at the University of Amsterdam Business School. Her research examines local, industry-specific firm competitive dynamics using archival, experimental and qualitative methods. Her work has studied the French bread market, the Dutch cannabis coffeeshop industry, and Chicago movie theatres during the transition to sound. Her research has appeared in Administrative Science Quarterly, Organization Studies and Harvard Business Review. She is a member of the Amsterdam Young Academy, a 2024 fellow of the Netherlands Institute for Advanced Study, and a recipient of an NWO Veni grant.

name: Juliane Reinecke
bio: Juliane Reinecke is Professor of Management Studies, Academic Area Head for Research, and Faculty Director for Sustainability at Saïd Business School, University of Oxford. She uses qualitative methods to study the emergence and transformation of sustainable industries, including food, garments, minerals and energy, and the roles of collective action, social movements, multi-stakeholder collaboration and transnational governance. Her work has appeared in leading management journals. She received her MPhil and PhD from the University of Cambridge and previously held professorships at King's College London and the University of Warwick.

name: Simon Bachelor
bio: Simon Bachelor is Head of the Drones Programme at British Transport Police, leading the development of drone capabilities to improve safety, security and operational efficiency across the UK's rail network. He oversees the delivery of the Beyond Visual Line of Sight programme and works with the Civil Aviation Authority, Network Rail and industry partners. With more than 30 years of policing experience, he has held operational, strategic, counter-terrorism and national-security roles, including work with the Home Office Counter Drones Unit and the National Police Chiefs' Council's Counter Drones portfolio.

name: Sofia Stayte
bio: Sofia Stayte is Head of the Aviation Skills and Future of Flight Branch within the UK Department for Transport's Aviation Safety, Innovation and Skills Division. She leads policy development at the intersection of emerging aviation technologies, workforce capability and regulation, including drones, advanced air mobility and future-flight systems. Her government experience spans pensions, skills and employment policy, rail workforce strategy, aviation Brexit negotiations and aviation consumer policy. She is a member of the Government Policy Profession and the Chartered Institute of Public Finance and Accountancy.

name: Dr Katie Hore
bio: Dr Katie Hore is Innovation Director at REWIRE, the UK's Innovation and Knowledge Centre for next-generation power semiconductors. REWIRE brings together the Universities of Bristol, Cambridge and Warwick with industry partners to accelerate the development and commercialisation of ultra-wide-bandgap semiconductor devices. She has more than a decade of semiconductor-industry experience spanning power electronics, optoelectronics and quantum technologies, and holds a DPhil in Chemistry from the University of Oxford.
